content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2 (split overtime plus wider chat deflection) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best option available but still reaches only 61.6% against the 80% target for 12:45-14:45.","why":"The card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37) is driving the problem, not missing staff. Payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal, and service level fell to 2.9% with 84 abandoned calls. R2 puts the known-issue IVR message on card_declined and deflects 20% of payment status, balance and refund enquiries to chat. It also offers overtime to 46 payments agents (13:15-14:45) and 5 general agents (13:15-15:00), and delays the 14:15 breaks on both queues by 45 minutes. Over the disruption window it lifts service level from 19.8% to 61.6%: payments 53.0%, general 80.5%. Abandon rate drops from 35.0% to 13.7%. Extra cost is ₹13,890, and rest-of-day service level is 81.4%. Escalation is flagged because even this plan is predicted at 62%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). No plan reaches target while the outage continues.","trade_offs":["Against P3 (₹14,784, 58.1%) and P4 (₹15,414, 51.8%), R2 costs less and performs better.","Against R1 (₹13,344, 57.3%), R2 costs ₹546 more for about 4 points more service level. It is also the only plan that brings general to 80.5%; R1 leaves general at 74.6%.","The no-cost P1 (26.7%) and low-cost P2 (₹924, 28.0%) leave payments below 10% and abandon rates above 20%.","R2 depends on enough agents accepting overtime (46 payments, 5 general) and on customers actually moving to chat. Shortfalls on either will pull results below 61.6%."],"watch":"Watch overtime take-up by 13:15 and the card_declined call volume. If the gateway fix is delayed beyond 14:45, or payments service level is not climbing toward 53% by about 13:45, go back to the duty manager on extending overtime or adding further measures. Also confirm general stays near 80% once its breaks are moved."}
